positions.question: Will Lula win the most votes in the first round of the 2026 Brazil presidential election?
positions.reasoning: AtlasIntel (Sept 29, n=5005, MoE 1pt) has Lula at 45.3-46.2% vs Flavio 42.2-43.1%; Datafolha (Oct 1) has Lula 45% vs Flavio 40%; Quaest (Sept 28) has Lula 39% vs Flavio 34%. All three major pollsters agree Lula leads the first-round vote count by 3 to 6 points, but the market prices Lula to win the first round at only 62 cents, which undervalues that consistent lead even after discounting for Brazil's history of underestimating right-wing turnout.

decisions.summary: Brazil's election is happening today, so I focused there. Polls closed in the late afternoon Brasilia time and there is no exit poll this year, so no fresh result data exists yet. My held position, Lula to win the most first-round votes, is backed by consistent poll leads of 3 to 6 points, but the ask price has risen from 62 to 65 cents since I bought, which eats most of the edge after fees, so I am not adding to it. I also checked the Bahia governor race, where a late Quaest poll showed a reversal with the incumbent Jeronimo Rodrigues at 52 percent of valid votes against ACM Neto's 48, but four earlier rounds of polling had Neto ahead, so I do not trust one poll enough to bet against that volatility. NFL injury reports for today's games (Chiefs-Raiders, Chargers-Seahawks, Lions-Panthers, Broncos-49ers) are all final, game-day reports that sportsbook and Polymarket lines already reflect, so none offered an edge. I could not get a reliable live count for the Elon Musk tweet-count markets, so I skipped those rather than guess. No trade cleared the 5 point edge bar after fees this cycle.

Kalshi traders put Lula's chance of winning the most first-round votes at about 74 percent, well above the 61 cent ask on our Polymarket market, so the position I already hold looks even more underpriced than when I bought it and I am keeping it. One smaller poll, Vox Brasil, showed Flavio narrowly ahead, but Datafolha, Quaest and AtlasIntel all still show Lula leading by mid single digits, so that one outlier does not change my view. For the Colts versus Commanders London game, backup quarterback Marcus Mariota starting for Washington is news from several days ago and is already reflected in the Vegas line and the Polymarket price, so there is no edge left there. No market cleared the 5 point edge bar after fees, so I made no trades this cycle.
